g.title: mlsys.feedback-delay->mlsys.loop-stability-margin
g.text: spends, at a rate set by the

a.xlink:title: The total delay around the sense-compute-communicate-actuate loop, which erodes a controller's stability margin and adds motion before any response can begin, so it must be budgeted end to end rather than stage by stage.
A justified execution-time upper bound under specified hardware and execution assumptions.
Selecting inputs using measured or estimated deviation from desired behavior.
The state and clearance conditions within which a specified stopping response remains feasible.
A qualification ladder that runs the real software, then real hardware, against simulated or recorded environments before physical trials.
Transfer of control between an automated system and a human operator, bounded by human reaction time, situational awareness, and mode clarity.
A timer that a monitored component must refresh within a deadline or window; expiry triggers a defined safe response such as reset or revoking control authority.
Software connecting sensing, perception, planning, and control processes as nodes that exchange typed messages over publish-subscribe topics with configurable delivery and timing policies.
The share of a robot's sense-to-act deadline allotted to sensing and perception, which bounds model size, input resolution, and frame rate on the onboard computer.
Having sensors or peripherals write input directly into model input buffers by direct memory access, avoiding CPU copies between capture and inference.
The delay from an interrupt request to the start of its handler, which contributes to event-response time alongside handler execution and subsequent processing.

A high-priority task blocked on a resource held by a lower-priority task while a medium-priority task preempts the holder, so the high-priority task's blocking time is unbounded and can exceed its deadline unless the scheduler bounds it.
A device network engineered to provide bounded delivery under stated traffic and scheduling assumptions, whose cycle time and occupancy constrain sensing and control deadlines.
The allowed gain or phase variation before a specified feedback loop becomes unstable, used to budget delay and model uncertainty around an operating point.

Feedback control that regulates the relationship between motion and contact force, by commanding a virtual stiffness and damping or by tracking a force setpoint, so a robot can touch, push, and insert without the force spikes that pure position control produces at contact.
